newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt seen failing business - poll.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt seen failing business - poll.

text.p: Australian company chief executives feel the Liberal-National government has little understanding of their needs and is failing to provide the vision that it should, according to a poll released on Thursday.
The Business Review Weekly magazine December quarter poll found only 29 percent of 151 chief executives surveyed rated the government's performance as good.
This compared with 52 percent of the 150 chief executives surveyed in the September quarter poll who rated the government's performance as good or very good.
"None considered the government to have done a very good job (in the December quarter)," the report said.
"This is a 23 percentage point drop in its approval rating."
The poll found that the proportion of chief executives who thought the government had done a bad or very bad job rose to 12 percent in the December quarter from seven percent previously.
Those that rated it as average climbed to 58 percent in the December quarter from 41 percent previously.
However, the poll found that the loss of confidence in the government was not matched by a rise of confidence in the Labor Opposition.
Those that ranked the opposition's performance as good or very good rose to five percent from three percent previously.
"Chief executives clearly were thinking that the government's poor performance reflected a fundamental problem," the report said.
"When asked to rate the government's understanding of the needs of business, only one percent considered it as very good and 28 percent as good.
"About half said it was average and 17 percent said poor or very poor."

The poll found that 89 percent of chief executives felt the government should have a clearly defined vision for industry, although when asked if the government had such a vision, 70 percent said no and 23 percent said yes.
"The shift in attitude toward the government is made more remarkable by the bullish outlook that chief executives said they had for the coming year," the report said.
The poll found 54 percent expected better business conditions in the next 12 months, while only six percent thought conditions would deteriorate.
